title: Motor Overload / Over-Current
shortDescription: Motor drew more current than the safety threshold allows.
fullDescription:
Waring commercial blenders (MX, CB15, Xtreme MX1500XTX) monitor motor current. E1 trips when the motor is stalled by overloading the jar with ice or frozen product, a bent blade, or a locked bearing. The controller cuts power to protect the motor.

This is the most frequent fault in smoothie and bar operations because inexperienced users over-fill the jar with frozen ingredients and too little liquid.

causes.cause: Jar over-filled with ice or frozen fruit

fixSteps.title: Cool and reset
fixSteps.instruction: Power off 10 minutes; motor overload needs to cool before reset.

fixSteps.title: Reduce load
fixSteps.instruction: Use Waring recipe guide — add liquid first, then frozen ingredients. Use pulse to break up.

fixSteps.title: Inspect blade/coupling
fixSteps.instruction: Remove jar, spin blade by hand. Check drive coupling for stripped splines.

whenToCallPro: Call pro if motor needs service — brushed/brushless motor work inside a sealed base.

faq.a: No — overload protects against motor burnout.

title: Motor Over-Temperature
shortDescription: Motor winding temperature sensor exceeded cutout threshold.
fullDescription: E2 indicates the motor thermistor has reached thermal cutout — usually from repeated heavy blending without rest. Waring rates most commercial blenders for ~3 minutes continuous duty; back-to-back heavy smoothies will overheat.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Let base cool 15-20 minutes before retry.

fixSteps.title: Clean cooling vents
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum bottom and side vents of the base.

whenToCallPro: Call pro if E2 recurs after cooling and cleaning.

faq.a: High-volume smoothie shops typically have 2-3 to rotate.

title: Jar / Lid Interlock Fault
shortDescription: Jar not fully seated or lid not detected.
fullDescription: E3 fires when the magnetic or mechanical jar-seated interlock does not confirm the jar is locked on the base. Waring adds this to prevent startup with a loose jar which could throw hot contents.

causes.cause: Jar not rotated into locked position

fixSteps.title: Reseat jar
fixSteps.instruction: Remove jar, align arrow with base mark, twist until click.

fixSteps.title: Verify magnet
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect jar base for missing interlock magnet and glue in if loose.

faq.q: Can I use a third-party jar?
faq.a: Only Waring OEM jars have the correct magnet alignment.

title: Speed Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Motor RPM not matching commanded speed.
fullDescription: E4 on Xtreme models (variable-speed) indicates the tach sensor is not reading motor RPM correctly. Could be a failed Hall-effect sensor, damaged magnet ring, or stretched belt (on belted models).

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Base disassembly needed for sensor replacement.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

faq.a: On MX series yes; on smaller models often replace the unit.

title: Keypad / Membrane Switch Failure
shortDescription: Keypad reports stuck or shorted button.
fullDescription: E5 indicates the controller detects a keypad button stuck closed on startup — usually from liquid intrusion under the membrane.

fixSteps.title: Dry out keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Leave powered off 24 hours in dry environment.

fixSteps.title: Replace keypad
fixSteps.instruction: OEM keypad overlay; base partial disassembly.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

faq.q: Can I pressure wash the base?

title: Sound Enclosure Interlock (Acoustic Blenders)
shortDescription: Acoustic shield not closed on sound-enclosure models.
fullDescription: E6 applies to Waring acoustic models (Sound Shield series). The clear cover must be fully closed for the motor to run — reduces noise in cafes. E6 means the interlock does not see the shield latched.

fixSteps.title: Close shield fully
fixSteps.instruction: Firmly close acoustic cover until click.

fixSteps.title: Adjust hinge switch
fixSteps.instruction: Per service manual, adjust switch arm.

faq.a: No — noise is the point, plus ingredient safety.

title: Controller Communication Fault
shortDescription: Display and main control board lost serial link.
fullDescription: E7 indicates a serial link failure between the HMI board and the motor controller board — usually a harness problem.
whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

faq.a: Check Waring 3-year commercial warranty on motor.

title: Supply Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Incoming voltage too high or too low for safe operation.
fullDescription: E8 protects the motor drive from surge or brownout. Brewery/bar circuits with heavy loads can drop voltage during compressor starts, triggering E8.

fixSteps.title: Check outlet voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Measure at receptacle with other equipment running.

fixSteps.title: Dedicated circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Have electrician pull a dedicated 20A circuit for the blender.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — licensed electrician for circuit work.

faq.a: Yes — a commercial-grade surge protector is worth installing.
